title: Softmax: Turning Attention Scores into Weights
objective: Show that in nanoGPT's manual attention path, `F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` turns each row of scaled, causally masked scores into non-negative weights that add up to 1. Masked (-inf) positions end up with zero weight.
audience_context: The learner is on the Attention concept, looking at CausalSelfAttention.forward in nanoGPT's model.py. The softmax call sits at line 69, inside the manual (non-flash) attention branch.
scope_note: 15 seconds is only enough for what softmax does to one masked score row and where it sits in the step order. I left out the internals of the flash path (`scaled_dot_product_attention`), the effect of attention dropout, why the scores are scaled by 1/sqrt(head size), and the exp/normalize arithmetic and numerical stability details.

evidence.excerpt:
# flash attention make GPU go brrrrr but support is only in PyTorch >= 2.0
        self.flash = hasattr(torch.nn.functional, 'scaled_dot_product_attention')

# causal mask to ensure that attention is only applied to the left in the input sequence
            self.register_buffer("bias", torch.tril(torch.ones(config.block_size, config.block_size))
                                        .view(1, 1, config.block_size, config.block_size))

else:
            # manual implementation of attention
            att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))
            att = att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))
            att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)
            att = self.attn_dropout(att)
            y = att @ v # (B, nh, T, T) x (B, nh, T, hs) -> (B, nh, T, hs)

branches.runs: model.py:62-64: y = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None, dropout_p=self.dropout if self.training else 0, is_causal=True)

claim_registry.text: On the branch where `self.flash` is false, `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` normalizes the attention scores along the last dimension. Each query row becomes a set of non-negative weights over key positions that sum to 1.

On the branch where `self.flash` is false, the steps run in this order: scores are computed as `(q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))`, then `masked_fill` sets positions where `self.bias` is 0 to `float('-inf')`, then `F.softmax` runs, then `self.attn_dropout`, then `y = att @ v`.

On the branch where `self.flash` is false, `self.bias` is a lower-triangular (`torch.tril`) mask. Future positions get -inf before softmax, so softmax gives them zero weight and each token attends only to itself and earlier tokens.
When `self.flash` is true, the explicit `F.softmax` line does not run. Instead, `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., is_causal=True)` computes attention in a single call.

must_show: The code line `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)`, labeled as being in the `else` (manual, `self.flash` false) branch
One row of a small T×T score matrix with mixed raw values, some of them -inf in the upper-right (future) cells
That row turning into weights between 0 and 1 whose sum is visibly 1, with the -inf cells becoming 0
Normalization happening across each row (the last dimension), not down columns or over the whole matrix
A short step strip in order: scale → mask → softmax → dropout → att @ v, with softmax highlighted
A brief tag noting that the flash branch uses `scaled_dot_product_attention` instead of this line
must_not_claim: That `F.softmax` always runs, or runs in every forward pass, regardless of `self.flash`
That softmax runs before scaling or masking, or that masking happens after softmax
That dropout comes before softmax, or that `att @ v` comes before softmax
That softmax normalizes down columns (over queries) or over the whole matrix instead of along dim=-1 per row
That softmax selects only the single largest score (a hard argmax) instead of producing graded weights
That masked positions are deleted or removed from the matrix rather than kept with weight 0
That softmax changes which scores rank highest in a row
That softmax is applied to the values v or directly produces the output y
visual_direction: Begin on the highlighted softmax line inside the manual branch, then zoom into one query row of the score matrix. Show it as a transformation: raw scores of very different sizes, with -inf cells dimmed, reshape into proportional weight bars that fill a single total of 1. Larger scores take larger shares, and the -inf cells shrink to nothing. Keep attention on that one row so the row-wise (dim=-1) direction is obvious, then briefly show every row normalizing the same way. Finish by pulling back to the ordered step strip, with softmax lit between mask and dropout and a small side tag pointing to the flash alternative.
